title: Theorems, proofs, and computation
text:
Theorem environments

Theorem (Fundamental theorem of calculus). Let \(f : [a,b] \to \mathbb{R}\) be continuous. Then for every \(x \in (a,b)\), \[
\frac{d}{dx}\int_a^x f(t)\,dt \;=\; f(x).
\]


Proof. Fix \(x \in (a,b)\). For \(h \neq 0\) small enough that \(x+h \in (a,b)\), \[
\frac{1}{h}\int_x^{x+h} f(t)\,dt \;-\; f(x)
\;=\;
\frac{1}{h}\int_x^{x+h} \bigl(f(t) - f(x)\bigr)\,dt.
\] The right-hand side is bounded in absolute value by \(\sup_{|t-x| \le |h|} |f(t)-f(x)|\), which tends to \(0\) as \(h \to 0\) by continuity of \(f\).


Definition. A function \(f: \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}\) is Lipschitz if there exists \(L \ge 0\) such that \(|f(x) - f(y)| \le L|x-y|\) for all \(x, y\).

title: Theorems, proofs, and computation
text:
Computation
We can run code right inside a post. Here’s \(\sin x\) alongside its degree-5 Taylor approximation:

import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

x = np.linspace(-np.pi, np.pi, 200)
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 3))
ax.plot(x, np.sin(x), label=r"$\sin x$")
ax.plot(x, x - x**3/6 + x**5/120, "--", label="Taylor (deg 5)")
ax.legend()
ax.grid(alpha=0.3)
ax.set_xlabel("x")
plt.show()




\(\sin x\) vs. its degree-5 Taylor polynomial at \(0\).




The approximation is excellent near \(0\) and visibly drifts as \(|x|\) approaches \(\pi\) — which is the whole point of a local Taylor expansion.
